transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (NovaPath - Head of ML), Sara Lee (NovaPath - CTO), Derek Yuan (NovaPath - Procurement)

Summary (auto): We scoped POC success criteria and workload sizing. Discussed pilot credits, stub SOW, timeline to procurement. Security questions (SOC2/KMS/VPC) noted; Redwood to share docs and run a controlled benchmark next week.

[00:00] Alex Kim (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time — appreciate it. Quick round robin, then we can get into the POC guardrails and what success looks like.
[00:18] Mark Rivera (NovaPath): Hey Alex, hi Priya. Long time, quick context — we're evaluating inference vendors for our summarization + rerank pipeline. Primary concerns are latency at scale and predictable cost.
[00:32] Priya Shah (Redwood): Great — can you give a sense for peak QPS and sequence lengths? That'll frame the benchmark plan.
[00:42] Mark Rivera (NovaPath): Baseline is 200 qps steady, but we need to handle spikes up to 30k qpm in batch bursts during nightly indexing; average sequence is ~350 tokens, sometimes up to 1k for long docs. Quality is priority for rerank accuracy.
[01:05] Sara Lee (NovaPath): And from a procurement/security angle: we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), KMS, and the option for VPC/private deployment. Also need contract terms that allow a short pilot (30 days) with credits.
[01:25] Alex Kim (Redwood): That's all doable. For the pilot we typically offer a credits package + a short SOW that defines success criteria. On the security side we have SOC 2 Type II, ISO, and can share KMS integration notes; private deployment is possible but takes more lead time.
[01:45] Derek Yuan (NovaPath): Curious on costs: what's the ballpark per-token economics for hosted vs dedicated for a workload like ours? We want to present numbers to finance.
[01:58] Priya Shah (Redwood): Ballpark — hosted is easiest for pilot; it has variable per-token costs. Dedicated gives better unit economics at sustained utilization. We'll send a slab/ballpark table but for sizing we need the exact QPS and RL (request length) distributions.
[02:12] Alex Kim (Redwood): For contracting path: typical flow is pilot -> pilot evaluation (benchmarks/pass-fail) -> procurement starts for dedicated or committed usage; we can provide an MSA + SOW and then schedule contracting. For small pilots we accept credit-based on-boarding instead of PO to accelerate.
[02:33] Mark Rivera (NovaPath): Ok, success criteria — we propose: P95 latency < 600ms for typical requests, cost target <$0.10 per 1k tokens for inference, and quality delta within 2% of our current baseline on rerank metrics. Does that map cleanly?
[02:58] Priya Shah (Redwood): Yes that's reasonable. We should run an A/B style benchmark: 1) latency/throughput sweep with synthetic load, 2) real dataset quality eval against your test prompts, 3) cost estimate from actual tokens consumed during the run.
[03:16] Alex Kim (Redwood): We'll provision a pilot model variant within our hosted environment for the benchmark. If you require private VPC, that adds ~2-4 weeks prep, depends on approvals.
[03:30] Mark Rivera (NovaPath): We prefer hosted for speed, but want a clear path to private if security sign-off demands it. Also, can Redwood provide a performance profile matrix for the model variants? We want to know which models to test for costing.
[03:46] Priya Shah (Redwood): Yes, we'll send the Redwood-verified performance profiles and recommended quantization options. Note: quantization can change quality slightly — we'll include recommended guardrails for that.
[04:00] Derek Yuan (NovaPath): On procurement cadence: we need SOW + pilot credit agreement to show finance. Is there a standard pilot credit size?
[04:12] Alex Kim (Redwood): Typical pilot credits for a POC of this scale are in the $10k-$25k range depending on benchmark depth. We can propose a 20k credit package that should cover the multi-day throughput runs and eval tokens.
[04:28] Sara Lee (NovaPath): For contracting, we need the SOW to list acceptance criteria and an exit clause. We also need clarity on data retention and audit logs.
[04:40] Priya Shah (Redwood): We'll include retention defaults and configurable retention windows. Audit logs and per-token tracing are available in Redwood Console; we can provide export formats for your SIEM.
[04:55] Mark Rivera (NovaPath): For the benchmark, can Redwood run a scheduled sustained load to validate autoscaling behavior? We care about tail latency under burst.
[05:07] Priya Shah (Redwood): Yes — we'll propose two phases: a spike test (simulate 30k qpm burst), and a soak test (48-hour steady run at expected steady qps). We'll instrument KV cache/prefix caching to see cost reductions.
[05:26] Speaker 1: sorry, real quick — when you say cache, do you mean the KV cahs?
[05:31] Priya Shah (Redwood): Yeah, sorry — KV cache, sometimes transcribed as K-V cash — prefix caching can dramatically cut token costs for repeated prefixes. We'll include a guidance doc.
[05:44] Derek Yuan (NovaPath): Any competitors we should be aware of? We're evaluating Anthropic and Bedrock. How does Redwood position on cost predictability?
[05:55] Alex Kim (Redwood): We emphasize predictable economics via dedicated pools and explicit batching/cache levers; unlike some fully managed endpoints, you can pick dedicated capacity to get unit pricing guarantees. We'll send a comparison sheet (not a formal RFP replacement).
[06:10] Mark Rivera (NovaPath): Ok, timelines — we want the pilot completed and evaluated within 30 days. Is that feasible?
[06:18] Alex Kim (Redwood): For hosted pilot yes — 30 days is doable. Private/VPC would extend timeline. Contracting and procurement can run in parallel; we'll provide an SOW and start the benchmark once the dataset and success criteria are confirmed.
[06:31] Priya Shah (Redwood): Actionables: we need the test dataset or sample prompts, and the exact success metrics. Also, provide the contact for procurement (Derek) so we can share draft SOW/credit agreement.
[06:45] Mark Rivera (NovaPath): I'll share a redacted test set and the rerank eval scripts.
[06:52] Derek Yuan (NovaPath): I'll circulate procurement cadence and get an initial PO estimate if needed.
[07:00] Alex Kim (Redwood): Great. On security docs, we'll attach SOC2 and our ISO summary, and an ops note on KMS/HSM integrations. Any specific compliance regime beyond that?
[07:12] Sara Lee (NovaPath): Also regulatory logs retention for 7 years for certain clients, so retention windows matter.
[07:20] Priya Shah (Redwood): We can configure retention, but very long retention windows may need enterprise plans. We'll spell out tradeoffs.
[07:30] Mark Rivera (NovaPath): One more: can Redwood run the benchmark with our rerank metric instrumentation so we get apples-to-apples numbers?
[07:38] Priya Shah (Redwood): Yes — we'll ingest your eval harness and run the quality tests. We'll also provide a result notebook with P95/P99 latency, throughput breakdown, token counts, and a cost estimate.
[07:50] Alex Kim (Redwood): OK to summarize next steps?
[07:55] Mark Rivera (NovaPath): Go ahead.
[07:57] Alex Kim (Redwood): We'll: 1) Send pilot credits agreement + SOW template (Alex) 2) Redwood will propose two benchmark windows and a plan (Priya) 3) NovaPath to share test dataset and success criteria (Mark) 4) Procurement to confirm timeline (Derek) 5) Redwood to send SOC2/ISO + KMS/VPC notes (Alex). Expect docs in 24–72 hours.
[08:24] Derek Yuan (NovaPath): Sounds good. Will finance need an initial quote? If yes, we request a simple hosted vs dedicated side-by-side for the expected steady/peak mix.
[08:36] Alex Kim (Redwood): We'll include a ballpark hosted vs dedicated comparison in the package. It won't be a final legal quote but should be enough for finance to sign off on pilot.
[08:46] Sara Lee (NovaPath): If pilot looks good we'll fast-track procurement for a committed Dedicated pool.
[08:51] Alex Kim (Redwood): Understood. Any blockers left?
[08:55] Mark Rivera (NovaPath): None from engineering.
[09:00] Derek Yuan (NovaPath): Procurement needs the SOW and a pilot credit agreement to start internal approvals.
[09:06] Alex Kim (Redwood): We'll prioritize that. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-words (KV cahs / K-V cash) and speaker labels simplified. References to shared artifacts: Redwood will attach: performance_profiles.pdf, pilot_sow_template.docx, SOC2_summary.pdf, benchmark_run_plan.xlsx.

Recap (auto): Pilot credits suggested ~$20k, hosted pilot in 30 days, benchmarks to cover spike and soak tests, success criteria to be finalized by NovaPath (latency P95, cost per 1k tokens, quality delta). Redwood to send docs and benchmark plan; NovaPath to share test dataset and procurement timeline.
